front.summary: Most are not emergencies; find the ones that are

back.body: THE QUESTION: did it build up, or was it at its worst STRAIGHT AWAY? · 'Worst headache of my life' — believe it, especially from a frequent sufferer · FEVER + STIFF NECK = CNS infection, precautions · Any FOCAL DEFICIT, seizure or altered mental status · AFTER A HEAD INJURY, especially older or ANTICOAGULATED — mechanism need not look impressive · Wakes from sleep · worse on straining · new over 50 · CARE: dim, quiet, gentle, position of comfort, transport

front.title: Insulin and glucose
front.summary: Fuel and the key to the door

back.body: GLUCOSE = the fuel · INSULIN = the key that lets it into cells · No key → glucose piles up in the blood WHILE THE CELLS STARVE · A HIGH READING DOES NOT MEAN FUELLED CELLS · The BRAIN fails first: no stores, no quick alternative → sugar problems look like brain problems · TYPE 1 makes none · TYPE 2 responds poorly and MAY STILL TAKE INSULIN · DOWN: medication without food, exertion, alcohol · UP: illness, infection, missed medication, stress
back.why_it_matters: A diabetic with flu usually runs high. The reflex expects low.

front.summary: Fast and sweaty, or slow and dry

back.body: SLOW onset: hours to DAYS · THE THREE POLYS: polyuria · polydipsia · polyphagia · PROFOUNDLY DEHYDRATED — glucose spills into urine and drags water with it · SKIN WARM DRY FLUSHED (mirror of hypo) · DKA: no usable glucose → burns FAT → ACID → DEEP SIGHING RESPIRATIONS blowing it off + SWEET/FRUITY BREATH · THAT BREATHING IS COMPENSATION — support it, never slow it · HHS: extreme glucose + profound dehydration, NO ketones, older type 2, slower still · CARE: airway, oxygen, position, TRANSPORT — fluid and insulin are not yours
back.why_it_matters: It looked like a respiratory call. The breathing was the only thing keeping his blood from turning to acid.

back.why_it_matters: They did not diagnose anything. They said the word steroid at handover, and that was enough.

front.title: Allergic reaction vs anaphylaxis
front.summary: It is not about the rash

back.body: ALLERGIC REACTION = immune overreaction · ANAPHYLAXIS = the same thing gone BODY-WIDE · THE LINE IS AIRWAY, BREATHING OR CIRCULATION — NOT how bad the rash is · Skin only, however dramatic = allergic reaction · Swelling, stridor, hoarse voice, wheeze, low pressure, collapse = ANAPHYLAXIS · Gut symptoms + skin after exposure = ANAPHYLAXIS · ABOUT A THIRD HAVE NO RASH AT ALL — that is how it gets missed · A sense of impending doom is a real finding
back.why_it_matters: She was wheezing with not a mark on her, and the absence of hives was doing the reassuring.

back.body: COMMON TRIGGERS: foods (nuts, shellfish, egg, milk, wheat) · insect stings · medications · latex · Route matters less than expected: eaten, injected or touched · BIPHASIC = a second wave HOURS LATER with NO further exposure, can be as bad or worse · THIS IS WHY EVERY ANAPHYLAXIS PATIENT IS TRANSPORTED, however well they feel · PAST MILD REACTIONS PREDICT NOTHING · Ask what and how long · Bring the packaging, device or medication
back.why_it_matters: Feeling better is what happens between the two waves.

back.body: FOUR ROUTES: ingestion · inhalation · injection · absorption · INGESTION IS SLOWEST — a well-looking patient early after swallowing means NOTHING · INHALATION AND INJECTION ARE FASTEST · ABSORPTION KEEPS WORKING until the substance is off them — DECONTAMINATION IS TREATMENT WITH A CLOCK ON IT · DO NOT ENTER an enclosed space that dropped somebody — rescuers become patients · FIRST TWO ACTIONS: stop the exposure, protect yourself · ASK: what, how much, when, what route, what was already done · TAKE THE CONTAINER
back.why_it_matters: Two people down instead of one, and the second did what anybody would instinctively do.

back.body: THE TRIAD: reduced consciousness · slow or absent breathing · PINPOINT PUPILS · THE BREATHING IS WHAT KILLS, NOT THE DRUG · SO VENTILATE FIRST — BVM before naloxone, every time · Naloxone displaces the opioid off its receptors · IT CAN WEAR OFF BEFORE THE OPIOID DOES → respiratory depression can RETURN · TRANSPORT EVERY NALOXONE PATIENT, however awake · Waking can be abrupt, frightened, combative — physiology, not character · Synthetics may need repeats per protocol — KEEP VENTILATING
back.why_it_matters: His colour came back before the naloxone was out of its packet.

front.title: Naloxone
front.summary: Never a substitute for a bag-valve mask

back.body: See the drug card fields. CLASS: opioid antagonist · INDICATION: suspected opioid overdose with respiratory depression · ROUTE: intranasal or auto-injector at EMT level, per protocol · SIDE EFFECTS: abrupt withdrawal, agitation on waking, vomiting, RETURN OF RESPIRATORY DEPRESSION as it wears off · DOSE: PER PROTOCOL — VERIFY, not stated here

back.body: STIMULANTS: fast pulse · high pressure · DILATED pupils · hot skin · agitated, paranoid → DANGERS ARE HYPERTHERMIA, SEIZURES, CARDIAC EVENTS in the young — TAKE A TEMPERATURE · SEDATIVES: drowsy · slurred · uncoordinated · SLOW SHALLOW BREATHING · SEDATIVE + ALCOHOL = far worse than either alone, both depress breathing · ALCOHOL IS A SEDATIVE OVERDOSE, not a behaviour problem · WITHDRAWAL CAN BE WORSE THAN INTOXICATION: tremor, hallucinations, SEIZURES · Glucose + injury check on EVERY intoxicated patient · NEVER RESTRAIN PRONE — positional asphyxia
back.why_it_matters: Either one alone he would have slept off. Together was why he was not breathing.

front.title: Carbon monoxide and cyanide
front.summary: The oximeter will lie to you

back.body: CO binds haemoglobin FAR more readily than oxygen → lungs work perfectly, nothing arrives · A PULSE OXIMETER CANNOT TELL THEM APART — A NORMAL READING MEANS NOTHING · SUSPECT FROM THE STORY: headache, nausea, dizziness, confusion, NO fever · MORE THAN ONE PERSON IN THE BUILDING · better away from home · ask about the pets · CHERRY-RED IS LATE AND UNRELIABLE · TREAT: out of the building + HIGH-FLOW O2 · CYANIDE: stops cells USING oxygen, from enclosed-space fires and burning synthetics · Fire victim, sooty, confused, not improving on O2 = SUSPECT BOTH
back.why_it_matters: Four people with headaches in one house, all reading 99 percent.

front.title: Carbon monoxide: what the numbers are worth

back.body: PULSE OXIMETER: UNRELIABLE — cannot distinguish carboxyhaemoglobin, a normal number excludes nothing · OXYGEN: high-flow, non-rebreather, after removal from source · CHERRY-RED SKIN: late and unreliable, do not wait for it · TRIGGER: more than one person affected in the same building · BINDING AFFINITY vs oxygen: far greater — the usual quoted multiple is deliberately NOT stated here, confirm it from your text
back.why_it_matters: The only number on this card you should trust is the number of people with a headache.

front.title: Organophosphates
front.summary: Everything wet, and the lungs are the emergency

back.body: IN PESTICIDES AND NERVE AGENTS · Every gland switches on at once · SLUDGEM: Salivation · Lacrimation · Urination · Defecation · Gastric upset · Emesis · Miosis · DUMBELS adds the letter that matters: BRONCHORRHOEA · THE LUNGS FILLING WITH THEIR OWN SECRETIONS IS WHAT KILLS · TREAT: SUCTION, VENTILATE, SUCTION AGAIN — relentlessly · The pupils are a clue, not the emergency · THEY WILL CONTAMINATE YOU: gloves, gown, eye protection · REMOVE AND BAG CLOTHING — it keeps dosing them · DECONTAMINATE BEFORE LOADING · Antidotes are outside EMT scope in most systems
back.why_it_matters: The pupils were a clue. The fluid coming up the tube was the emergency.

front.title: Poison control and charcoal
front.summary: Call early, and put very little in mouths

back.body: POISON CONTROL: contact EARLY per protocol, en route if you can · HAVE READY: substance · quantity · time · weight · the container · ACTIVATED CHARCOAL: binds some swallowed substances — used FAR LESS than it once was, time-limited, protocol-driven · DOES NOT BIND alcohols, acids, alkalis, iron, lithium · CONTRAINDICATED: unprotected airway · cannot swallow · falling consciousness · corrosives · hydrocarbons · CHARCOAL IN THE LUNGS IS ITS OWN SERIOUS INJURY · DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING — ipecac is obsolete
back.why_it_matters: Could this person's consciousness drop in the next twenty minutes? If maybe, nothing goes in the mouth.

front.title: Abdominal pain assessment
front.summary: Watch the face, palpate the sore bit last

back.body: FOUR QUADRANTS · OPQRST — PROVOCATION and RADIATION carry the information · VISCERAL = dull, crampy, waves, a flat hand rubbing a region · PARIETAL = sharp, constant, ONE FINGER ON ONE SPOT · VISCERAL → PARIETAL IS A DETERIORATION, not clarity · REFERRED: SHOULDER TIP = blood or air under the diaphragm · PALPATE THE PAINFUL QUADRANT LAST, watch the FACE · EPIGASTRIC PAIN CAN BE CARDIAC — older patients, women, diabetics · NOTHING BY MOUTH · position of comfort · NEVER HEAT
back.why_it_matters: She kept rubbing a shoulder nothing had happened to. It was reporting on her abdomen.

back.body: PERITONITIS: RIGID, board-like · LIES ABSOLUTELY STILL, knees up · every bump hurts · stop pressing once you have the finding · APPENDICITIS: vague pain AT THE NAVEL → MIGRATES to RIGHT LOWER QUADRANT over hours · fever, vomiting, off food · SUDDEN RELIEF = RUPTURE, NOT RECOVERY · OBSTRUCTION: crampy WAVES · distension · vomiting, may become faeculent · NOTHING PASSING · gets dry fast · ALL THREE: nothing by mouth, comfort, watch for shock, transport

front.title: Gastrointestinal bleeding
front.summary: The bowl is not the measurement

back.body: UPPER vs LOWER · Vomited BRIGHT RED = fast upper bleed · COFFEE GROUNDS = blood that sat in stomach acid = upper · BLACK TARRY STOOL = digested blood = ALSO UPPER · Bright red from below = lower, OR a very brisk upper bleed moving fast · WHAT YOU SEE TELLS YOU ALMOST NOTHING — most of it is still inside · ASSESS FOR SHOCK INSTEAD: pulse → skin → mental status → PRESSURE LAST · ASK: anticoagulants, liver disease, alcohol · Suction ready · keep WARM · nothing by mouth · GO
back.why_it_matters: A small amount in a bowl, a pulse of 116, and a perfectly normal blood pressure.

back.body: GALLBLADDER: RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT · often 1–2 h after a FATTY MEAL · colicky, patient may be restless · may refer to the RIGHT SHOULDER BLADE · PANCREAS: upper/central, BORES THROUGH TO THE BACK · constant and severe · WANTS TO SIT UP AND LEAN FORWARD, flat makes it worse · associated with ALCOHOL and GALLSTONES · Both vomit, both get dry · DO NOT TRY TO TELL THEM APART — same care: nothing by mouth, THEIR position of comfort, shock watch, transport
back.why_it_matters: He was not being difficult. Lying flat was the one position that made it unbearable.

front.title: Varices and dialysis patients
front.summary: Suction out, and never that arm

back.body: VARICES: liver back-pressure swells veins at the base of the food pipe → RUPTURE = SUDDEN, BRIGHT RED, MASSIVE · CAN KILL IN MINUTES · THE AIRWAY IS THE THREAT, NOT THE VOLUME · SUCTION OUT AND TESTED BEFORE YOU WALK IN · They clot badly — the liver makes the clotting factors · DIALYSIS: missed sessions → FLUID OVERLOAD (breathless, swollen, cannot lie flat) and RISING POTASSIUM (fatal rhythms, no warning) · ASK WHEN THEY LAST DIALYSED · NEVER a BP cuff or anything else on the FISTULA ARM · Bleeding fistula = FIRM CONTINUOUS PRESSURE, do not lift to look
back.why_it_matters: Four words changed the handover: when did you last dialyse?
